message:
In the twin under-deck retrofit concept, the damper tuning approach has a 1.86 hertz versus 1.81 hertz inconsistency. To check it I used a whiteboard cross-check (the Den Hartog optimum result (E3)). I found 1.81 hertz tuning differing by 0.05 hertz from the inspiration optimum, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose Structural Dynamics Lead, please reconcile mass ratio and optimum formula for the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD). My position: not ready because tuning basis is unresolved.

In the concealed twin-unit support concept, the clamp-beam and spring static method has missing load-path quantification. To check it I used a process review (the concealed mounting detail sketch (E9)). I found 250 kilogram hung units with 20.0 millimetre dynamic travel but no static sag or bolt load in newtons, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose Retrofit Integration Architect, please compute beam stress, U-bolt slip margin and spring sag with clearance. My position: not ready because support safety objection remains open.

In the crowd comfort verification concept, the acceptance method has target drift from Comfort Level (CL) CL1 to Comfort Level (CL) CL2. To check it I used a target comparison (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found 0.74 metres per second squared exceeding the 0.5 metres per second squared CL1 limit, according to Setra, 2006. I propose Pedestrian Comfort and Construction Planner, please confirm whether CL2 is accepted with Vibration Control Specialist. My position: not ready because ready claims precede agreed target.

Note on Structural Dynamics Lead: tuning reconciliation requested.
Note on Vibration Control Specialist: effective damping claim needs agreed target.
Note on Retrofit Integration Architect: static load-path calculation requested.
Note on Pedestrian Comfort and Construction Planner: CL1 versus CL2 acceptance requested.
